solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Whale in two locations near Ibiza

definitions.text: Whale in two locations near Ibiza

parts.words: Whale in two locations near Ibiza
parts.note: the whale's four letters end the names of the two larger Balearic islands, Ibiza's neighbours, so they lie in two locations

explanation.surface: A whale has been spotted at two places off the coast of Ibiza.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'locations' are not sea positions but island names: Majorca and Minorca, Ibiza's Balearic neighbours, both end in the four letters wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: The killer whale is a large black-and-white toothed cetacean, so it is a whale by species.

clue.text: Embarrassed Dickensian character is keeping quiet? The opposite

indicators.note: keeping says one piece holds another inside it, here between character and quiet
the surface says the character keeps quiet; 'The opposite' reverses who holds whom, so the quiet word goes round the character and 'is'

parts.note: SH is the call for quiet
Uriah Heep is the creeping clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a Dickens character is embarrassed into keeping quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The opposite' tells you to swap container and contents from the surface reading: the quiet word holds the character, not the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sheepish looks abashed and awkward, the same as being embarrassed.

clue.text: Drunks turned up holding up vessels in church

indicators.note: holding means the reversed drunks contain the next piece
in a down clue the word for drunks is turned, read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: sots are habitual drunkards
taken as written

explanation.surface: Drunkards rolled up in church clutching the holy-water vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reads as one phrase but splits: 'turned' is the reversal signal and 'up' supplies its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoup is a basin for holy water near a church door, a kind of vessel found in church.

clue.text: What's naughty about maiden, maybe being put in reduced circumstances

indicators.note: about means the naughty word goes round the other piece

parts.note: impish describes something mischievous or naughty
in cricket a maiden is an over with no runs scored, so it is one example of an over

explanation.surface: A mischievous act involving a young woman leaves someone struggling financially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maiden' is the cricket term: a maiden over is a set of six balls from which no runs are scored. 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To impoverish someone is to make them poor, reducing them to straitened circumstances.

clue.text: Military officer, post-war planner seen as inadequate

indicators.note: inadequate means falling short, so the planner's name lacks its final letter

parts.note: George Marshall devised the Marshall Plan to rebuild Europe after the Second World War

explanation.surface: An army officer criticises the architect of post-war recovery as not up to the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen as inadequate' cuts the last L from MARSHALL.
explanation.definitionFit: A field marshal is the highest army rank, and marshal names a senior officer in many forces.

clue.text: Dull thing to discuss — no conclusion reached

indicators.note: with no conclusion the word for a topic loses its final letter

parts.note: a matter is a subject or issue for discussion

explanation.surface: A tedious topic is debated and nobody reaches a decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no conclusion reached' drops the final R of MATTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A matte finish is flat and lacking shine, so dull in the sense of not glossy.

clue.text: Characters not flustering when losing one legal document

parts.note: letters are written characters of the alphabet

indicators.note: losing means the calm word must give up a letter

parts.note: someone patient stays calm and does not get flustered
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Written words that don't rattle anyone describe a calm legal paper, minus a detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when losing' takes I (one) out of PATIENT, leaving PATENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters patent are an open royal or government document granting a right, title or monopoly.

clue.text: Tongue as starter for meal in train

indicators.note: in means the first letter goes inside the train

parts.note: the train of a dress or comet is its trailing tail

indicators.note: starter for means the opening letter of the word meal

explanation.surface: A dining-car passenger is ordering a starter in their own language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter for' gives M, which goes inside TAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue means language; Tamil is spoken in southern India and Sri Lanka.

clue.text: Spirit being overcome by sin — it extends over a few years

definitions.text: it extends over a few years

indicators.note: in a down clue the spirit lies below the sin, so it is overcome by it

parts.note: lust is one of the seven deadly sins
rum is a distilled spirit

explanation.surface: Drink gets the better of someone, and the indulgence goes on for years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being overcome by' works only in a down entry, where the sin sits physically on top of the spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A lustrum is a period of five years, originally the Roman census cycle.

clue.text: Line of planks in slope at end of street

indicators.note: at end of puts the slope after the street

parts.note: a rake is a slope, as of a theatre stage

explanation.surface: A row of boards lies on an incline at the far end of the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at end of' is a positional signal: the slope comes after the street abbreviation; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: On a boat a strake is one continuous row of planking running from bow to stern.

clue.text: French city trip curtailed by unpleasant person

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, so the trip loses its last letter

parts.note: a tour is a trip or journey
a louse is a contemptible person

explanation.surface: A holiday in France is cut short because of an obnoxious companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' is literal: cut off the tail, the last letter, of the trip word.
explanation.definitionFit: Toulouse is a large city in south-west France, on the Garonne.

clue.text: A sneer — this destroyed enthusiasm

indicators.note: destroyed means the letters of a sneer this are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone's scornful sneer has crushed another's zeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' rearranges A SNEER THIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartiness is warm, vigorous keenness, so it matches enthusiasm.

clue.text: Say in course of story-telling what befalls poor team?

indicators.note: in course of means the example sits inside the narration

parts.note: a relation is a telling or narration of a story
EG, for example, is what 'say' means when introducing an instance

explanation.surface: Someone, while telling a story, mentions what happens to a struggling football team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in course of' is the container signal; the question mark flags a definition by example, since dropping to a lower division is what befalls a team near the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A team that finishes near the bottom of a league is demoted to a lower division at season's end.

clue.text: Wild animal — a particular continent's rhino

definitions.meaning: the wallaroo, a large Australian kangaroo, is also called by this name
rhino is old slang for money, and this is Europe's common currency

explanation.surface: A wild beast is described as one continent's rhinoceros.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rhino' is not the animal but old British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: The currency of most of the European Union, and separately an Australian wallaroo.

clue.text: Country's beginning to mushroom — so Scotsman introduced population theory

indicators.note: introduced means the next pieces are put inside the country and initial

parts.note: Mali is a West African country; with the 's it gives MALIS
thus means so, therefore
Ian is a typically Scottish man's name

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of the word mushroom

explanation.surface: A nation's growth begins to balloon, so a Scot is brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' picks the first letter of mushroom; 'introduced' puts the so-word and the Scot inside the country-plus-initial, splitting it after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Malthus argued that population grows faster than food supply, and this doctrine bears his name.

clue.text: Detective starts to learn some snippets

parts.note: Inspector Morse is the Oxford detective of Colin Dexter's novels and the TV series

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letters of the words learn and some

explanation.surface: A detective begins to pick up a few scraps of information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes L and S from 'learn some'. 'Morse' is the Oxford detective of British TV.
explanation.definitionFit: Morsels are small bits, mouthfuls or fragments, so snippets.

clue.text: Special vessel NASA's newly developed in Land of Opportunity

parts.note: Noah's ark is the special vessel of Genesis

indicators.note: newly developed means the letters of NASA's are rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: NASA has built an unusual craft in a land where anyone can succeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly developed' rearranges NASAS into ANSAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Land of Opportunity is the official nickname of the US state of Arkansas.

clue.text: Quiet trick from one who feels no guilt?

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
to rig is to manipulate or fix by trickery

explanation.surface: A quiet deception comes from someone with no conscience.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: a prig is so self-righteous they never feel guilty.
explanation.definitionFit: A smug moralist thinks themselves above reproach, so never feels guilty.

clue.text: Bird's first need having flown north — possible site for nest?

indicators.note: the bird's first means the opening letter of the word bird

parts.note: lack means need or want

indicators.note: flown suggests the letters of north have flown about and landed in another order

explanation.surface: A bird's first priority after migrating north is finding a nesting spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having flown north' reads as migration, but 'flown' is the anagram signal acting on 'north'.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorny hedge shrub, sloe-bearing, where birds often build nests safe from predators.

clue.text: Rail against educationist that's made a mistake

parts.note: to boo is to jeer at or protest against
a BEd, Bachelor of Education, is the degree a trained teacher holds

explanation.surface: Someone protests against a teacher who has got something wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: B.Ed (Bachelor of Education) stands for the educationist.
explanation.definitionFit: To boob is British slang for to blunder, so it means erred.

clue.text: Bottomless foundation? Gosh, it's very big!

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of the foundation word is its last letter, which goes

parts.note: a root is the base or foundation, as of a tooth
my is an exclamation of surprise like gosh

explanation.surface: Someone peers into a pit with no bottom and exclaims at its size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottomless' removes the final T from ROOT, the bottom of the word in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Roomy means spacious, with plenty of room, so generously large.

clue.text: Something sweet, additive mostly included in medicine?

indicators.note: included in means the shortened additive goes inside the medicine

parts.note: a dose is a measured amount of medicine

indicators.note: mostly means the additive loses its last letter

parts.note: an extra is something added

explanation.surface: A sweetener is added to medicine, perhaps to help it go down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of the additive word; 'included in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dextrose is a form of glucose, a sugar, hence something sweet.

clue.text: Variation in game needing cue

parts.note: nim is a game of taking matchsticks or counters from heaps
a cue is a rod used in snooker or billiards

explanation.surface: A twist on a sport that requires a snooker cue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variation' is a capitalised musical work: Nimrod is the ninth of Elgar's Enigma Variations.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgar's Enigma Variations include one named after the biblical hunter, a famous slow movement.

clue.text: Suitable food, for non-vegetarian, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is identified by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: meat is flesh food eaten only by those who are not vegetarian

explanation.surface: Someone says this dish is appropriate for a meat-eater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns MEAT into the like-sounding archaic adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Meet is an old word for fitting or proper, as in 'meet and right'.

clue.text: Sweep of eras looking back, hard to avoid

indicators.note: to avoid means the hard letter is left out
looking back means the word for eras is read in reverse

parts.note: epochs are eras, long periods of history
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A survey of past ages, steering clear of the difficult bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking back' reverses EPOCHS to SHCOPE; 'to avoid' removes H.
explanation.definitionFit: Scope means range or extent, the full sweep of something.

clue.text: Rugby success — one's getting on in this sort of play

indicators.note: in means the old word sits inside the rugby score

parts.note: a try is the score made by grounding the ball in rugby
getting on means growing old, so aged

explanation.surface: A rugby win where an older player triumphs becomes the stuff of drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'one's' and 'this' are only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedy is a drama with an unhappy ending, one genre of stage play.
